title: Shorter signup form
hypothesis: If we reduce the signup form from eight fields to four, more people will create an account because the form requires less effort.
control: The current signup form with eight fields.
treatment: A four-field form. Ask the remaining questions after account creation.
population: New people starting signup. Assign a stable variant before displaying the form. Define staff and bot exclusions before assignment.
metric_definition: People who create an account within one day / all unique people assigned to the variant.
baseline_source: Illustrative assumption: 20%. Measure this population and outcome window before running a real test.

guardrails.name: Activation within seven days
guardrails.definition: People who complete their first key action / all people assigned to the variant.
guardrails.limit: If B shows a statistically significant drop against A after full follow-up, hold the rollout and investigate.

blockers: Confirm the baseline conversion rate and the flow of new unique people.
recommendation: Revise this plan. Confirm the baseline first. At these illustrative numbers, traffic is insufficient to detect an increase from 20% to 21% in 14 days.
decision_rule: After the planned horizon and full follow-up, assess the effect, uncertainty and activation. An inconclusive result does not establish success. A significant primary improvement alone does not authorize rollout.
